In step 4, I'm going to investigate the clusters identified by the clustering algorithm.  
 - How similar or dissimilar are they with respect to the primary topics (and the fields and subfields to which those topics belong) 
 - What are the most important works for each cluster based on page rank and betweenness.
 
To simplify this process, 
 
Workflow:
Step 1)  Add attributes in the node-list for the network characteristics:  cluster membership, page rank, and betweenness metrics.  [This was done in "04a_cluster_nodelists.rmd".]

Step 2) Explore the new node-list.
  
  a) overall descriptions of works (journal source, source group)
  b) group by cluster and summarize to compare average page rank and betweenness
  c) for each cluster, look at the primary_topic variables ==> FOR LOOP!!
  

 Step 3) extracting information from the new node-list

  * find the papers with the highest page-rank and betweenness metrics
  * use "highest" variable to find the works in each group with the highest page-rank values
       
       
```{r 3) extracting specific works based on network}

imp_works_insular_prank <- met_insular  |>  
  group_by(cluster) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = prank, n = 1) |> 
  select(sid_prank = source_id, 
         sg_prank = source_group, 
         wid_prank = work_id, 
         doi_prank = doi, 
         title_prank = title, 
         pubyear_prank = publication_year, 
         citedby_prank = cited_by_count, 
         fwci_prank = fwci, 
         pt_prank = primary_topic,
         pt_sub_prank = primary_topic_subfield, 
         pt_field_prank = primary_topic_field, 
         pt_domain_prank = primary_topic_domain,
         cluster,
         prank)

imp_works_insular_btw <- met_insular  |>  
  group_by(cluster) |> 
  slice_max(order_by = btw, n = 1) |> 
  select(sid_btw = source_id, 
         sg_btw = source_group, 
         wid_btw = work_id, 
         doi_btw = doi, 
         title_btw = title, 
         pubyear_btw = publication_year, 
         citedby_btw = cited_by_count, 
         fwci_btw = fwci, 
         pt_btw = primary_topic,
         pt_sub_btw = primary_topic_subfield, 
         pt_field_btw = primary_topic_field, 
         pt_domain_btw = primary_topic_domain,
         cluster,
         btw)
  
# using "bind_cols" on these didn't work because there were tie values in some clusters
  # which made the columns unequal in length

# too lazy to add "na" values and make them the same length

# Google ai said to try the following, but it was definitely mistaken - not in the package
    # install.packages("qpcR")
    # library(qpcR)

imp_works_insular <- merge(imp_works_insular_prank, imp_works_insular_btw)

# this will work - can go back in and easily correct the duplicate values

# saveRDS(imp_works_insular, "data/important_works_insular.rds")

output_directory <- "C:/Users/Owner/Documents/Research/R_Projects/nais_ps/data_output/"
file_name <- "Important_Works_insular_20261002.csv"
full_output_path <- file.path(output_directory, file_name)

write_excel_csv(imp_works_insular, file = full_output_path)

```


Step 4) visualize the network and use different node attributes

```{r 4) network visualization}

# Got some visualization code from Sara!  

ggraph(cit_graph_big, layout = "fr") +
geom_edge_fan(
end_cap = circle(1, "mm"),
color = "#000000",
width = 0.3,
arrow = arrow(angle = 15, length = unit(0.07, "inches"), ends = "last", type = "closed"))+
geom_node_point(alpha = 0.2) +
labs(title = "NAIS-themed Citations (insular network)") + theme_void()

```
